In the morning, clouds drift down between the treetops, moss covers the damp trunks, and the trail disappears into lush greenery. Chicaque offers a day in an Andean cloud forest just outside Bogotá. Visitors walk the trails, watch birds, and reach natural viewpoints.

The park has trails of varying difficulty. Ascents and descents make the walks active, so comfortable footwear and preparation for wet weather are useful even on a short route. Horseback riding and ziplining are also available as park activities; their scope and availability are confirmed separately from standard admission.

On the Ada Tours itinerary, the walk is accompanied by a local guide and ends with a traditional lunch. Chicaque complements the capital's museums and historic neighborhoods: a single outing reveals another side of Colombia, filled with forest air, mist, and mountain scenery.

Chichén Itzá is on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula. The archaeological site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In different periods, the complex was an important Maya center and later came under Toltec influence.

Stone structures from different eras survive here. Exploring them offers an insight into how the region's architecture changed over time. A visit is often combined with a stop at the Ik Kil cenote.

### Chichicastenango — A Market Town!

Chichicastenango lies in a picturesque valley beneath the looming Chichi Mountain, 120 km northwest of Guatemala's capital. Despite its relative isolation from the outside world, the town is an important trading center where Indigenous people from across Central America bring their crafts to sell.

Its main attraction is the country's largest market, described by some sources as the largest in all of Central America. Locals call it "Chichi." It operates two days a week, on Thursdays and Sundays. On Sundays, a religious procession passes along the main street toward the church, after which chickens are sacrificed. Flowers are sold on the steps of the church, which was built on the ruins of a Maya pyramid.

## Visiting Chichicastenango Market

### The "Chichi" Market Welcomes Visitors!

"Chichi," which locals call the largest market in the country and, according to some reports, all of Central America, opens twice a week, on Thursdays and Sundays. Stalls sell traditional clothing, amulets, Maya ritual masks, scarves, woolen blankets and bedspreads, and a variety of souvenirs. Everything is bright and unusual. The pleasant climate makes a market visit especially enjoyable, while several historic churches are among the town's defining landmarks.
